data.narrative:
Proxima Fusion is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised €145M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 total entities across nuclear energy: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Fuse Energy, Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Oklo. The three most directly comparable peers in stage and sector are Valar Atomics (Series B, $6.0B), Nano Nuclear Energy (Seed, $808M), and Fuse Energy (Series A, $200M).

Two primary valuation methods apply. The stage-progression method uses total capital raised ($145M) as a base proxy and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $290M. The peer-median approach across the three comparable companies produces $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. This wide dispersion reflects material heterogeneity in stage and market positioning within the nuclear energy frontier-tech space.

Triangulation of these two methods supports a valuation range of $246M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $549M. The considerable spread between methods—$290M versus $808M—reflects fundamental uncertainty in stage-comparable peer selection and the nascent state of commercialization timelines in fusion and advanced fission. Key uncertainties include regulatory pathway clarity and capital efficiency relative to peer trajectories.
